title: LR with Mandatory Shot-Quality Features — Sub-0.20 Brier Target
source: MDPI Information 17(1):56 (Jan 2026) — Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets
key_finding: Logistic Regression with team-level metrics + Elo ratings + rolling-form indicators + spatial shot-chart embeddings achieves Brier 0.199 and outperforms XGBoost (0.202) on Brier/log-loss while XGBoost retains AUC edge. Shot-chart ablation shows consistent degradation in BOTH discrimination and calibration when removed.
why_novel: All 6 existing islands use tree-based models only. LR has not been tested as a standalone model type in the GA. The 2026 study's key insight is that LR's linear probability outputs are inherently better calibrated than tree models, and when combined with shot-quality spatial features it achieves best-in-class Brier without any post-hoc calibration.

proposed_changes.change: Add 'logistic_regression' to MODELS list in ga_config
proposed_changes.rationale: LR is CPU-fast, inherently calibrated, achieves 0.199 Brier in 2026 study

proposed_changes.change: When model_type == logistic_regression, enforce minimum 10 shot_quality features (Cat42)
proposed_changes.rationale: 2026 study confirms shot-chart spatial features are critical for LR calibration

expected_improvement: Brier improvement of 0.01-0.02 (from 0.220 toward 0.199) based on 2026 study results on similar game count (9,551 games)
implementation_effort: LOW — 2 code changes, ~20 lines, no new data required
validation: Run LR on current best feature set (S14: 59 features, extra_trees → 0.22006) and compare Brier
